newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa seeks changed close corporation rules.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa seeks changed close corporation rules.

text.p: South African Trade and Industry Minister Alec Erwin on Tuesday published a draft law to refine laws governing close corporations.
The bill, which has still to be passed by the parliamentary committee on trade and industry, proposes changes to the liability and responsibility of members of a close corporation.
A close corporation is a corporate entity that is cheaper and simpler to register than a company.
Changes highlighted in a memorandum explaining the proposals include:
- "It is made clear that a member's interest in a close corporation is movable property, subject to attachment and may be sold in execution.

- "...any act of any member of a close corporation binds the close corporation unless the member concerned has no power to act in the particular matter and the person with whom he or she deals has or ought to have knowledge that such a member has no sch power."
- The registered name of a close corporation must be translated into any one of the country's 11 official languages, but need not appear specifically in English and Afrikaans.
- The liability of a member who did not deliver his member's contribution is limited to the period in which he or she was in default.
- Provision is made for a close corporation in financial difficulties to seek an offer of composition or any other arrangement acceptable to its creditors.
